articles.title: Got Rs 5,000 but don't need it? Maharashtra minister urges farmers to return aid - India Today
articles.summary: Got Rs 5,000 but don't need it? Maharashtra minister urges farmers to return aid India Today
articles.content: Maharashtra minister Girish Mahajan on Saturday urged financially well-off farmers who do not need government support to return the Rs 5,000 drought relief payment to the Chief Minister's Relief Fund, news agency Press Trust of India reported.The state government recently announced advance assistance of Rs 5,000 each for eligible farmers in drought-affected areas ahead of Diwali.“Those who do not need the money should voluntarily return the Rs 5,000, considering it as a contribution towards helping farmers who are in need. My appeal is to everyone who is financially capable,” Mahajan, the state's disaster management minister, told reporters in Jalgaon district.Mahajan said several farmers and party workers from his constituency approached him on Saturday morning and said they wanted to return the assistance because they did not need it. Around 50 farmers had expressed their willingness to return the money as they were financially secure and had other sources of income, he told PTI.“I will appeal to people to stand firmly behind our food provider, the farmer, during such difficult times and extend financial assistance through the Chief Minister's Relief Fund,” he said, adding that he would personally approach people in this regard.The Devendra Fadnavis government on October 27 approved Rs 7,500 crore in assistance for farmers in 304 drought-hit talukas. Farmers whose crops suffered damage of more than 33 per cent were eligible for the relief, which was to be transferred directly to their bank accounts.Relief and Rehabilitation Minister Makarand Jadhav Patil said on Friday that the state had transferred Rs 4,372.83 crore to the bank accounts of 87,45,669 farmers as of November 5, according to PTI. Assistance to the remaining eligible beneficiaries was being processed, while authorities worked to resolve technical issues and discrepancies in bank account details that had delayed some payments.The assistance is part of the Maharashtra government's response to drought conditions and crop losses during the Kharif season, while Mahajan's appeal seeks voluntary contributions from farmers who are financially secure to support those in need.- Ends

articles.title: Watch | Para-powerlifter Ashok Malik gifts churma to PM Modi during felicitation event, video goes viral - Livemint
articles.summary: Watch | Para-powerlifter Ashok Malik gifts churma to PM Modi during felicitation event, video goes viral Livemint
articles.content: Prime Minister Narendra Modi met India's para-athletes in New Delhi on Thursday (5 November), congratulating them on their record-breaking performance at the 2026 Asian Para Games in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan.During the interaction, Modi was also seen feeding para powerlfter Ashok Malik a spoonful of churma, a moment that featured in a video shared on social media. Ashok had brought a box of churma for PM Modi, who in return offered the athlete a spoon of the sweet dish. Ashok won silver in the men's 65kg para powerlifting event at the 2026 Asian Para Games. The meeting took place at the Indira Gandhi Sports Complex in New Delhi, where Modi interacted with members of the Indian contingent, their coaches, trainers and families. The interaction was held after India's best-ever campaign at the continental para-sports competition, where the country secured 114 medals. India's 114-medal tally comprised 30 gold, 35 silver and 49 bronze medals. The performance surpassed the country's previous best of 108 medals at the 2023 Asian Para Games in Hangzhou, China. The Indian contingent also recorded five world records and nine Asian records in Aichi-Nagoya. PM Modi compares India's performance in 2010 and 2026Addressing the athletes, Modi drew a comparison between India's performance at the 2010 and 2026 editions of the competition, highlighting the progress made in para-sports over the years."Just think about this journey from fourteen to one hundred and fourteen. It is the result of the highest level of your hard work," Modi said.He also pointed out that 34 of India's 56 women athletes at the competition won medals. Indian athletes swept all three podium positions in four events, while the contingent secured nine gold medals on the final day of the competition.Modi highlighted the contribution of families, coaches and trainers to the athletes' achievements. He also referred to the journey of Rinku, who lost his mother two months before the competition but went on to win a gold medal. The athlete honoured her memory by lifting her photograph after his victory. "That moment touched the hearts of all Indians ," the Prime Minister said.He also praised the performances of athletes who made their debut at the continental competition. Of India's 61 debutants, 36 returned with medals, while Sandeep set a world record in his first appearance at the Games.“Your struggles and achievements are an inspiration to every Indian. And in this journey, your path and the nation’s path have been very similar. That is why today, your efforts and the efforts of the nation are combining and creating an even greater force together,” Modi said.PM Modi sets sights on Los Angeles 2028 ParalympicsThe Prime Minister also discussed India's preparations for the 2028 Los Angeles Paralympics, asking the athletes not to treat their Aichi-Nagoya achievements as the final destination."The podium at Aichi-Nagoya is not the final destination of your journey," he said, urging the athletes to use their success as a launching pad for bigger goals.He added that Avani and Manish had already secured quota places for the Los Angeles Games and called for greater Indian participation at the 2028 event.Modi also highlighted the contribution of government-backed sports programmes. Athletes supported under the Target Olympic Podium Scheme (TOPS) won 41 medals at the Asian Para Games, while Khelo India athletes contributed 19 medals.He said sports should be viewed as a means of character-building and nation-building, adding that they teach discipline and team spirit."Sports teach discipline and the meaning of team spirit," Modi said.The Prime Minister also referred to the government's approval of the Khelo India Sports Goods Manufacturing Scheme, worth more than ₹1,800 crore. He called for Indian sports equipment, apparel and footwear to reach international markets."We want India to produce not only world-class athletes but also world-class sports equipment," he said.Modi concluded by encouraging the athletes to celebrate their achievements while beginning preparations for their next challenge, reiterating that the country was behind them."The country stands with you, and so do I. The entire nation is waiting for your next victory," he said.

articles.title: Maharashtra CM Fadnavis Assures Farmers of Support Amid Drought Crisis - Asianet Newsable
articles.summary: Maharashtra CM Fadnavis Assures Farmers of Support Amid Drought Crisis Asianet Newsable
articles.content: Maharashtra Government Extends Support to Drought-Hit Farmers Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis said that at a time when the state is facing a natural calamity in the form of drought, the state government is standing firmly by the farmers. "Along with financial assistance, various schemes are being implemented to support those affected by the drought. Several more schemes will be introduced in the coming period, and all of us will have to face this natural calamity unitedly, " his office said in a release. CM Devendra Fadnavis was addressing villagers after a prayer meeting organised by the Gurudev Seva Mandal in Lohari Savanga village of Nagpur district. The prayer meeting was held in the assembly hall on the premises of the Lohari Savanga Gram Panchayat. Revenue Minister and Nagpur Guardian Minister Chandrashekhar Bawankule, MLAs Charansingh Thakur, Ashish Deshmukh and Dr Rajiv Potdar, former MLA Sudhakar Kohale, District Collector Kumar Ashirwad, Zilla Parishad Chief Executive Officer Vinayak Mahamuni and other senior officials were present along with Chief Minister Fadnavis. Government Measures and Relief Schemes While interacting with the villagers, CM Fadnavis said, “This has been a year of challenges. The rains remained elusive until the very end. As a result, crops were damaged and farmers suffered enormous losses. In some parts of the state, serious shortages of fodder and even drinking water have emerged.” He said that during this difficult period, the state government has stood firmly behind the farmers. “Some time ago, the government took the major decision of farm loan waivers and helped farmers get back on their feet. Lakhs of farmers benefited from the loan-waiver scheme. However, the drought situation has once again created a crisis for farmers. Therefore, the state government has now extended direct assistance to them,” he said. The Chief Minister said that to enable farmers to celebrate Diwali, the government has deposited Rs 5,000 into the bank accounts of around 1.5 crore farmers. "The process of depositing the money is still underway." He added that farmers’ electricity bills have been waived, along with outstanding electricity bill arrears. "Several schemes have also been introduced to provide relief to the rural population, while more schemes will be implemented in the coming period," his office said. Future Infrastructure and Community Support “Water conservation works will be undertaken on a large scale. Efforts will also be made to address various issues, including people’s health concerns,” the Chief Minister said. Chief Minister Fadnavis further said that he and his colleagues had come to the village with the objective of spending the Diwali festival in a manner that would give courage and reassurance to farmers facing difficulties. Referring to the teachings of Rashtrasant Tukdoji Maharaj, his Gramgeeta and his devotional songs, the Chief Minister said, “There is tremendous strength in Rashtrasant Tukdoji Maharaj’s bhajans. Even when a person is deeply distressed during difficult times, the thoughts of the Rashtrasant give him the strength to rise again. The teachings of Gramgeeta can make villages prosperous in every respect.” He added that the Rashtrasant’s thoughts on what should be done during a drought are highly inspiring and provide clear direction. “May the thoughts of Gurudev also give all of us the strength to face this crisis,” Chief Minister Fadnavis said. articles.title: Maharashtra Govt Eases Farmer ID Registration and Crop Inspection Rules - Asianet Newsable
articles.summary: Maharashtra Govt Eases Farmer ID Registration and Crop Inspection Rules Asianet Newsable
articles.content: New Measures for Farmer ID and Crop Registration The Maharashtra government has announced a series of measures to facilitate Farmer ID registration and crop inspection for farmers across the state, with Revenue Minister Chandrashekhar Bawankule taking the initiative to ensure that eligible farmers are not deprived of government benefits due to gaps in land records or cultivation information. Under the new procedure, farmers who could not obtain a Farmer ID under the Agristack initiative due to the non-availability of land records or cultivation details will now be able to get their records verified by the Talathi, Mandal Officer and Tehsildar. In another decision, the Revenue Department has issued a circular introducing an alternative procedure for crop inspection where online Kharif crop registration is not possible due to technical or geographical difficulties. Such crop inspections will now be conducted through 'e-Ferfar', with the process being undertaken at the Talathi level to ensure that crop registration is not stalled. The decision is expected to provide relief to around 70 lakh farmers in the state. Bawankule has instructed the Revenue Department to implement the new procedure. The initiative aims to ensure that all farmers can avail themselves of the benefits of government schemes, subsidies, crop loans, crop insurance and digital agriculture services. Government Support Amid Agricultural Challenges Meanwhile, Maharashtra Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis, addressing reporters, said the current year had been challenging due to inadequate rainfall, which resulted in heavy crop losses and problems related to fodder and water availability. He said the government was standing firmly with distressed farmers and had initiated several measures, including depositing Rs 5,000 each into the bank accounts of 1.5 crore farmers. The government has also decided to waive outstanding electricity bills amounting to Rs 58,000 crore up to June. Fadnavis said the government had decided to celebrate Diwali with farmers to encourage them amid the difficulties. He also highlighted plans to construct check dams, small water barriers and undertake water conservation projects to address water scarcity in villages. The Chief Minister further said that various healthcare facilities, including free surgeries, were being provided and assured farmers that the government would stand behind them to ensure access to these services. articles.content: Chennai SQUASH Velavan Senthilkumar bows out of London Open in quarters India’s Velavan Senthilkumar bowed out of the London Open after losing to French World No. 99 Amir Khaled-Jousselin in the men’s quarterfinals on Friday. World No. 42 Senthilkumar, the second seed, went down 11-13, 6-11, 7-11 in what was a major upset at the USD 18000 PSA Challenger event. In-form Senthilkumar had won his second PSA Copper-level crown at the Czech Open earlier this week. -Team Sportstar ESPORTS India to compete in global championship of F1 Sim Racing The Indian simulator racing unit has earned a spot in the Cup of Nations that will see it compete with top international teams in the two-day global championship in Mumbai. The event, to be held from November 7-9, is organised by Mumbai Falcons Racing Limited in partnership with Formula 1. Representing India in the 18-team event will be Karl Verghese and Siddharth Sathgare, following the former’s crowning as the national champion in the Open Category at the F1 Sim Racing. Verghese finished with 150 points, while fellow Mumbaikar Siddharth Sathgare secured second place with 96 points and Chennai’s Amith Kutti finished third with 91 points. The podium finishers maintained their distance from the rest of the pack throughout the six-race competition. Karl remained unbeaten across all six races to establish his dominance in the category. -Press Trust of India ARCHERY Youth Olympics: Archer Gatha storms into pre-quarterfinals with straight-set win India’s lone archer Gatha Khadake made a confident start to her campaign at the Youth Olympics, cruising into the pre-quarterfinals of the women’s recurve under-18 event with a straight-set 6-0 win over Ivory Coast’s Sita Sore in Dakar on Saturday. The third-seeded Gatha was in complete control throughout the first-round contest, winning 28-21, 28-24, 28-19 to wrap up the match without breaking a sweat. The 16-year-old was consistent across all three sets, scoring 28 points each time and dropping just two points from her six arrows in every set. Sore struggled to keep pace, managing scores of 21, 24 and 19. Gatha opened with two 9s and a 10 to take the first set, 28-21. She followed it up with two 9s and an X in the second to extend her lead to 4-0. The Indian then completed the rout with an X, a 10 and an eight in the third set, while Sore managed just 19 points, including two fives. The archer from a village near Solapur in Maharashtra has already gained valuable international experience despite her young age, having made her senior debut at the World Cup Stage 4 in Madrid last year. She defeated Chinese Taipei’s Chiu Yi-Ching, a 2022 World Cup bronze medallist, to reach the pre-quarterfinals there. Her most notable performance came at the World Championships in Gwangju last year, where she made an impressive run to the fourth round. With experienced Indian archers Deepika Kumari and Ankita Bhakat having exited earlier, Gatha was the country’s last competitor in the fray before losing to Korean Olympic medallist Lim Sihyeon. Gatha will next face Bulgaria’s 14th seed Neda Kenderova in the round of 16 on Monday. -Press Trust of India CRICKET St. Froebel ends Modern School’s two-season unbeaten run, lifts 2026 Delhi Capitals School Cup St. Froebel Paschim Vihar brought an end to defending champion Modern School, Barakhamba Road’s remarkable unbeaten run across two seasons to lift the 2026 Delhi Capitals School Cup title with a comprehensive eight-wicket victory in the final at The Games Forest ground in Gurugram on Friday. Modern School, which had won all its matches in both the inaugural edition and the 2026 tournament leading up to the final, suffered its first defeat in two seasons in the title clash. However, a clinical bowling performance led by Karn Sharma, followed by a blistering batting display from opener Laksh Narang, ensured that St. Froebel produced a memorable upset against one of the tournament’s most dominant sides, chasing down a target of 56 in just 3.2 overs. Abeer Sudan of Billabong School, Noida, dominated the individual batting charts to claim the Orange Cap after an outstanding campaign in which he amassed 421 runs in five innings at a remarkable strike rate of 249 and an average of 210. He also topped the overall performance rankings and was adjudged the Most Valuable Player (MVP) of the tournament. In the bowling department, Vinayak of Modern School, Barakhamba Road, claimed the Purple Cap after finishing as the tournament’s leading wicket-taker with 15 wickets at an economy rate of 5.55. The Fair Play Award was presented to Billabong School, Noida, in recognition of the team’s sporting conduct throughout the tournament. The second edition of the Cup brought together 38 teams for 66 matches across four venues in the Delhi-NCR region. The tournament commenced on October 9 and culminated with the final on November 6. -Team Sportstar FOOTBALL Super League Kerala: Magic break the jinx Finally, after six games, Thrissur Magic has posted an outright win. For a team that played the Super League Kerala (SLK) football final last year, this has indeed been a season of disappointment. On Saturday night, in front of its fans who turned up in fairly large numbers at the Municipal Corporation Stadium, the Thrissur men beat Kannur Warriors 2-0. And it was to Kannur that they lost in the final last year. So, this victory would have pleased them immensely. Thrissur now has seven points, the same as Kannur. The two sides are at the bottom of the table, which has Calicut FC at the top with 14 points, followed by Forca Kochi (13), Malappuram FC (11) and Thiruvananthapuram Kombans (eight). Calicut and Kombans have played only six games each, one less than the others, and they come face to face at Thiruvananthapuram on Sunday. On this night, Thrissur was a deserving winner. The host had taken an early lead in the seventh minute through Valentine Ekejiuba. The Nigerian scored following a long ball from Sergio Gil; when the goalkeeper S. Hajmal fumbled, Valentine took advantage and celebrated the goal with a double somersault. Valentine had chances to score two more goals in the first half, though. But he had a hand in his team’s second goal; it was off his pass into the box that Silajit Santra scored. For the defending champion, it was a fourth straight loss. RESULT Thrissur Magic 2 (Valentine Ekejiuba 7, Silajit Santra 51) bt Kannur Warriors 0. -P.K. Ajith Kumar BEACH WRESTLING Taniya storms into beach wrestling final at Youth Olympics India’s Taniya stormed into the women’s 75kg beach wrestling final at the Youth Olympic Games, setting up a gold-medal clash with China’s Zhao Min after an unbeaten run in the competition in Dakar on Saturday. Taniya was in dominant form throughout the day, winning all four of her bouts to book her place in the title clash. She began her campaign with a 3-1 victory over Germany’s Mia Mauer in Group B, winning by technical superiority, before getting past Greece’s Vasiliki Karavanou by the same route in her second group bout at Saly Beach West. The Indian continued her impressive run in the knockout rounds, defeating Estonia’s Merily Vaester 4-1 by technical superiority in the quarterfinals before overcoming Matilda Ann Hruby of the United States 3-1 in the semifinals to seal her place in the final. Taniya will now take on China’s Zhao Min with a gold medal at stake. Beach wrestling, a fast-paced combat sport contested on sand within a seven-metre circular area, is making its debut at the 2026 Dakar Youth Olympic Games in Senegal. Each bout lasts a maximum of three minutes, with a wrestler declared the winner upon scoring three points or executing a decisive throw that lands the opponent on their back. -PTI RESULT Thrissur Magic 2 (Valentine Ekejiuba 7, Silajit Santra 51) bt Kannur Warriors 0.

articles.summary: Great Damage Done to India's Fabric Under Modi Govt: Sonia Gandhi Deccan Chronicle
articles.content: New Delhi: "Great damage" has been done over the last 12 years to the fabric of India, democracy and institutions, Congress Parliamentary Party Chairperson Sonia Gandhi has alleged, asserting that even after the Modi government goes, it will take time to restore the country's systems back to health.In an interview with The Hindu ahead of the launch of her book, 'Belonging: A Journey of Love', she also pointed out that people are now beginning to be restless and recognising the damage."But I am optimistic and I know that the people of India will welcome a return to proper governance," the former Congress chief said."Over the last twelve years great damage has been done to the fabric of our country, our democracy and our institutions. Even after this government goes, it will take time to restore our systems back to health and great effort from political parties," she said.Asked about the decline of the Congress and her assessment of its present condition and prospects, Gandhi said, "I am not so pessimistic. Consider that the Congress party and other opposition parties have not had a level playing field since this government came to power."Take into account the complete stranglehold they have on all institutions, especially the Election Commission, their control of mainstream media, their money power and their exploitation of religion.""Yet, our party is fighting and making progress; in fact, it is the only party that has had the resilience to withstand this onslaught," Gandhi said.She alleged that Congress workers and leaders "have faced persecution of all kinds"."And yet, in every village and every district, Congressmen and women are still fighting for the values enshrined in our Constitution," she said."What is more, it has been amply proved in recent months that many elections have been stolen, and people are now more aware of it," she alleged. "The Congress is working with like-minded parties, and our prospects are improving day by day," she said.'Belonging: A Journey of Love', published by HarperCollins India, is a personal memoir, with politics providing the background or "a kind of framework", as she puts it in the book.On Prime Minister Narendra Modi and what lessons the Congress should draw from his rise, Gandhi said, "It's true that he comes from a very different ideological world. But there are many ways that people succeed in politics within the Congress party, take for example Dr. Manmohan Singh and Congress President Mallikarjun Kharge. I don't think we have much to learn from the RSS."On whether she wonders how UPA policies and Congress strategy might have differed had she accepted to become prime minister in 2004, Gandhi said, "No, not at all. That has never crossed my mind. Our experience was by and large a very positive one. We worked as a team, and our roles were distinct, with him (Singh) leading the government and I leading the party."Last month, Sonia had said that others have spent decades telling her story and now it's her turn. She had also said there is bound to be some "tamasha" when her memoir comes out on November 10.HarperCollins India will publish Gandhi's 544-page memoir "Belonging: A Journey of Love" in India on November 10, ending the uncertainty over the book's domestic publication following an "impasse" between the author's representatives and Penguin Random House India (PRHI).PRHI, which was initially keen to publish the memoir, subsequently said it would not be the Indian publisher.The controversy began amid reports of differences between the publisher and the author's representatives over editorial changes to the manuscript.Several Congress leaders had raised issues of governmental pressure and freedom of expression with some alleging that there was pressure on Penguin India to remove sections relating to Prime Minister Modi, the RSS and China's "occupation" of Indian territory during the Modi regime.PRHI clarified that they were "really keen" to publish the book, describing it as a "hard-won acquisition", but ultimately decided to step away due to a "stalemate over a particular issue".While maintaining there was no external pressure whatsoever, PRHI declined to disclose the exact nature of the impasse, citing confidentiality clauses and their agreement with the author."Belonging" begins with Sonia Gandhi's childhood in post-war Veneto, Italy and traces her journey to Cambridge, where in 1965 she met Rajiv Gandhi.The memoir recounts her marriage to Rajiv Gandhi and her introduction to her mother-in-law, former prime minister Indira Gandhi, as well as her efforts to adjust to life in India, including learning Hindi, wearing saris and adapting to Indian food and culture.It covers the major tragedies that transformed the Gandhi family, including the death of Sanjay Gandhi in a plane crash, Indira Gandhi's assassination in 1984 and Rajiv Gandhi's assassination in 1991.The memoir also delves into political events surrounding the Congress-led alliance's victory in the 2004...

Consider that the Congress party and other opposition parties have not had a level playing field since this government came to power."Take into account the complete stranglehold they have on all institutions, especially the Election Commission, their control of mainstream media, their money power and their exploitation of religion.""Yet, our party is fighting and making progress; in fact, it is the only party that has had the resilience to withstand this onslaught," Gandhi said.She alleged that Congress workers and leaders "have faced persecution of all kinds"."And yet, in every village and every district, Congressmen and women are still fighting for the values enshrined in our Constitution," she said."What is more, it has been amply proved in recent months that many elections have been stolen, and people are now more aware of it," she alleged. "The Congress is working with like-minded parties, and our prospects are improving day by day," she said.'Belonging: A Journey of Love', published by HarperCollins India, is a personal memoir, with politics providing the background or "a kind of framework", as she puts it in the book.On Prime Minister Narendra Modi and what lessons the Congress should draw from his rise, Gandhi said, "It's true that he comes from a very different ideological world. But there are many ways that people succeed in politics within the Congress party, take for example Dr. Manmohan Singh and Congress President Mallikarjun Kharge. I don't think we have much to learn from the RSS."On whether she wonders how UPA policies and Congress strategy might have differed had she accepted to become prime minister in 2004, Gandhi said, "No, not at all. That has never crossed my mind. Our experience was by and large a very positive one. We worked as a team, and our roles were distinct, with him (Singh) leading the government and I leading the party."Last month, Sonia had said that others have spent decades telling her story and now it's her turn.
